pr_title: AEEncoderFFmpeg: Break when one packet is received
pr_comments: I suggest merging this fix to address the original issue and afterwards I will try my variants discussed in #22476
I can confirm that transcoding is working with these changes.  Thanks!
@basilgello Don't like the change anymore? Or forgot to reopen?
I want to clear Jenkins cache (see win-uwp logs)
@basilgello Could you add the LOG as discussed, then we could shuffle it in?
@basilgello https://github.com/fritsch/xbmc/commit/25d6e7c1ec4a0232355bc84598b027de974cd3a5 please force push that one and we are done. I incorporated the review comments requested by @lrusak
@lrusak Okay with you now? Please merge ahead if it is the case. Fixups are always possible.

> @lrusak Okay with you now? Please merge ahead if it is the case. Fixups are always possible.

Yea sure. My comments are resolved however I am always sceptical in merging code with the idea of an actual rework later.

Just looked again at the code. This needs a lot of rework in the way the decoder is called. So not really the way to handle EAGAIN to error out ... but rather to implement it with the possibility to properly react on EAGAIN, e.g. having more packages there, enqueueing them, coping with their PTS and especially with potentially multiple pakets on a later call, combined with the delay management.

The caller currently has an assumption: I get a single pkt or an error. The PR above realizes this design pattern and errors out when the constraint is not fulfilled.

In the chain that is happening - it's okay for me.
I am going to merge this by tomorrow. Reason: I want to unbreak current master. The Todo is in place, the assumptions are verified and the Error will directly tell us when things start to go wrong.
I superseeded this one, as it's only triple work to let my code ship in a different PR. Thanks much - all comments have been adressed.

Hmmm, all I can see in the log is this:
```
2023-01-08 21:44:48.707 T:19345   error <general>: CDVDAudio::AddPacketsRenderer - timeout adding data to renderer
```
@smf007 Can you post screenshots of relevant transcoding settings so I can reproduce the issue?

Settings are shown below.  These settings works fine with the Jan 5th build, prior to the pull.

![A059BC19-B9FB-4EFB-913D-DFE60E4C195B](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7517171/211247728-0541f11d-ff9a-4372-9bb9-a861c89703f8.jpeg)
![DA8D8F6B-2B0A-4C59-8BA7-CEF580C46BF8](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7517171/211247736-a3a05325-79b3-4674-ae99-4b8cbb20ea1c.jpeg)
I don't really know the code, but should https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Encoders/AEEncoderFFmpeg.cpp#L302 be a while loop?
Yes. Should be a while loop. It's the send / receive API, used in polling mode.

The previous code, using the older API, doesn't have that loop.  My question then is, how is the encoded packet then being transmitted on?  Would it not sit there in the loop until it finished encoding the whole audio stream?
No, it loops for receiver and the receiver puts out either one or two packets. At least, should work that way :)

So, avcodec_send_frame loads up a frame of audio.  avcodec_receive_packet spits back encoded packets.  When avcodec_receive_packet has nothing further to give, it should return a value to break the loop.

In this [stack overflow example](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59470927/how-to-replace-avcodec-encode-audio2-avcodec-encode-video2-with-avcodec-send), they are obviously writing out to file, but they are using that packet before unreferencing it.  If I'm mistaken, in Kodi now I don't see anything happening with the encoded packets.  What does variable pkt has after the while loop?  Wouldn't it be null?
Interesting point. I have just checked the extradata commit of the same chain and the pktRef received is used. Let me check the ffmpeg docs.

The https://ffmpeg.org/doxygen/4.0/group__lavc__encdec.html states tnat "Providing user-allocated buffers for avcodec_receive_packet() is not possible." but in trunk revision of the same page the whole example is omitted. It looks like we need to copy contents of `pkt->data` into `out` checking the size of all packets against buffer size.

I think the code currently expects pkt to be send back to the calling routine.
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Engines/ActiveAE/ActiveAE.cpp#L2277
That would limit to only returning 1 packet though.

Yes, that's the case: https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/xbmc/guilib/FFmpegImage.cpp#L702  - see also FFmpegPicture for the same. We were used to not allocate new memory for the output before, but this is now a change in the new API (several years old though), has hit us in ffmpeg picture before as well, via: https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/commit/4b8572a13810c3cc9ad88277c379d0f29770afd5

And while it is easy for the picture use-case: One input, one output. The AC3 encoder might output more pkts from one frame, therefore besides the missing copy, the while loop, though not being wrong, might only (after memcpy is fixed) deliver the last package before EAGAIN / EOF happens.

EAGAIN btw. is not an error, it just means: nothing here at this point, but might come later ... this was iirc invented when certain encoders / decoders work asynchroneously in the background to not block callers infinitely.

Which brings me to the discussion we had some years ago about our MP3 Encoder inside kodi, that the new API should be used in a way, that it brings benefit, not to try "wrapping old behaviour".

I'd better engage into automated functional testing discussion - it is definitely doable to capture audio, video and logs to catch at least "no sound" issues properly. Maybe we should think of it as a GSoC project?

Unfortunately that doesn't work.  My amp though shows 2 channels instead of none, but it's still not receiving anything.  Also no change in that the video works fine for a few seconds, then gets sluggish and eventually freezes.  Kodi then gets terminated.
https://paste.kodi.tv/firafuxobu.kodi

review_comments:
in this comination the while loop makes no sense, as it can always only go through this code exactly once:

1) proper package
2) EAGAIN or EOF
3) Error

so in this combination you can change the while to an if instead or consider my second try in the original thread, which was tested.
I simplified the commit and ensured there are no packet leaks thanks to early returns. Please test it again. @smf007 I will schedule an Android 32 and 64 build for you.
Yes. Will close this one and open a new one. Much easier than maintaining my change in another PR.

You cannot rely on the value of pkt->size, as you might never get a package. The stuff here works like this:
a) make a sane initial stage -> memset entire buffer
b) Copy the Buffer in, if we get one.

And
c) We break after first package received.

Your change would be perfectly right when we would expect more than one package, but then we also needed to check if it still fits.

I guess I don't follow. The memcpy() which follows relies on value of pkt->size

apologies if I am making amateur mistake/assumption

No, you have a point here. You don't touch the buffer if not packet is returned, therefore your save the memset. We play it safe and help us a bit with the debugger later on. 
Thanks for your comment.
